This skill is the shared floor, not the detailed framework playbook.
Use frontend-patterns for React, state, forms, rendering, and UI architecture.
Use backend-patterns or api-design for repository/service layers, endpoint design, validation, and server-specific concerns.
Use rules/common/coding-style.md when you need the shortest reusable rule layer instead of a full skill walkthrough.

facts.text: Deciding whether a piece of duplicated logic should be extracted under DRY or left alone because premature abstraction would cost more than the duplication does.

facts.text: Default to the simplest solution that works, KISS, and treat added complexity as something that must be justified by an actual current requirement, not a speculative future one, YAGNI.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Prefer self-documenting code with clear variable and function names over comments that explain what confusing code does; fix the naming first, comment only what the code can't say for itself.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Extract genuinely repeated logic into shared functions or components, DRY, but only once the duplication is real and recurring, not on the first sighting of similar-looking code.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Watch for named code smells, such as magic numbers, during review and replace them with named constants so the meaning of a literal value is documented at its point of use.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Over-engineering a solution for requirements that don't exist yet, violating YAGNI in the name of future-proofing.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Extracting an abstraction after seeing the same logic only once or twice, before the duplication is actually established, which tends to produce the wrong abstraction.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Optimizing code before establishing that the code path is actually a performance bottleneck, premature optimization, trading readability for speed nobody asked for.

facts.text: Relying on comments to explain what a poorly named variable or function does, instead of renaming it so the code documents itself.

facts.text: This skill is explicitly the shared floor, not the detailed framework playbook; it deliberately doesn't cover React, state management, or other framework-specific concerns, so applying it alone leaves real gaps for framework-heavy code.

facts.text: KISS, DRY, and YAGNI are principles that can conflict in practice, since a simple solution can also be a duplicated one, and the baseline doesn't resolve every such tension.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Self-documenting code is a default, not an absolute; some logic, such as a non-obvious business rule or a workaround for an external bug, genuinely needs a comment no naming scheme can replace.
facts.note: AI-suggested, synthesized from this pack's existing facts — not extracted from a source document.

facts.text: Code smell detection, like spotting magic numbers, catches surface-level issues but doesn't substitute for a deeper architectural review; a codebase can pass every smell check and still have a bad overall design.
